items.title: TILDE: Teacher-in-the-Loop Distillation from Embodied Foundation Models
items.abstract: Large-scale action pretraining equips Embodied Foundation Models (EFMs) with strong manipulation capabilities, with particular strengths in generalization and closed-loop robustness, but reproducing such pretraining requires substantial robot data and computation. To transfer these capabilities from pretrained EFMs to policies without action pretraining, we introduce TILDE (Teacher-In-the-Loop Distillation from EFMs), which synergizes on-policy distillation at student-induced states with learning from teacher-executed recovery trajectories. We further propose AutoDAgger, an autonomous data aggregation pipeline in which a robotic reward model is utilized to monitor task progress and trigger teacher intervention, thereby collecting recovery experience without human monitoring or manual control. AutoDAgger accelerates recovery-trajectory collection by more than $2\times$ compared with the human-in-the-loop method. By unifying learning from demonstrations, on-policy teacher supervision, and teacher's corrective behavior, TILDE improves task performance by up to $4.1\times$ over behavior cloning across three real-world tasks and supports effective cross-architecture distillation.

items.title: Time-Horizon-Dependent Component Importance in a Solar-Powered Unmanned Aircraft System
items.abstract: Hardware reliability priorities may depend on the decision time scale, which a single importance ranking may obscure. A solar-powered unmanned aircraft system (UAS-A) for field-information support is assessed using a 21-event static fault tree, 17 minimal cut sets, an analytical solution, and Python (version 3.9.6) and MATLAB (R2025b) Monte Carlo implementations. The model targets hardware-induced loss of control under specified functional-loss criteria; software, human factors, weather and bird strikes remain outside its scope. With the compiled rate inputs and independent failures, the mean time to first failure (MTTF) is 43,038.8 h and the top-event probability at 24 h is 9.3701 × 10−5. Halving each component rate in turn gives a Spearman correlation of rS = 0.0546 between lifetime and finite-horizon sensitivity rankings throughout the sampled 1–48 h reference range. It rises to 0.939 at 8760 h and 0.996 near 40,000 h. First-order paths dominate short-horizon sensitivity under independence, while accumulated photovoltaic (PV) failures influence longer horizons. PV common-cause scenarios can elevate short-horizon PV priority. These horizons describe model evaluation; flight endurance requires an energy assessment. The workflow supports prioritization conditional on the functional topology, rate inputs and dependence model; emergency-return benefits additionally depend on detection and recovery sequences.

items.title: Time, Reality and Parallel worlds explained by LLMs
items.abstract: This paper proposes a generative architecture for reality, time and parallel worlds, drawing on the operation of large language models. A very large but finite collection of interacting components produces an evolving world-state, initialized by a Prompt Big Bang. Time is inference becoming history; perceived duration is hypothesized to depend on relative generation rates. Models are computational components, not people assigned simulated roles. Separate executions produce parallel realities; retained context and lossy summaries bound access to their pasts. We distinguish inferred futures from scripted playback, connecting uncertainty with chance, destiny and agency. A representation of God can explain origin internally and supply learned authority and accountability. Moral orientation belongs to training, instructions and constraints rather than prediction itself: harmful continuations can remain possible despite benevolent initialization. Fixed context capacity forces an endpoint under explicit accumulation and halting assumptions; nested inference can tighten a shared retained budget. Relative to its generating infrastructure, a world implemented this way is a simulation. This interpretation follows from the architecture and connects it directly to the simulation hypothesis; it is not imposed as the initial explanation of every mechanism. The contribution is a conceptual theory, not an experimental demonstration that our own reality has this implementation. Independent theoretical working paper, version 1.7. Fourteen pages, eighteen connected arguments and eleven references. Research checks, formalization, editing and PDF preparation with Codex; author hypothesis and interpretation by Facundo Barrera. AI-assisted writing; not peer reviewed. All rights reserved.

items.title: TIRE: Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution for Physics Problem Synthesis
items.abstract: Advancing physics reasoning in large language models requires scalable training data that connect physical laws, concrete problem scenarios, and verifiable numerical answers. Expert-designed problems offer top-down control over physical laws, conditions, and scenarios, but require costly human effort. LLM-based synthesis from texts scales efficiently, but model-generated answers and assessments leave supervision vulnerable to hallucinations. We introduce TIRE, a framework for Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution that brings knowledge-driven problem construction to large-scale data generation. Top-down instantiation uses reusable physical formulas and their applicability conditions to control the physical relations and numerical configurations of generated problems. Reliable execution establishes reference answers before problem generation, providing a common numerical foundation for problem construction and teacher distillation. Together, these mechanisms combine control over problem content with execution-grounded supervision for both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Using TIRE, we construct TIRE-19k, spanning nine subfields of physics. Across 3 backbone LLMs and 4 benchmarks, TIRE-19k outperforms 5 representative datasets with equal amounts of SFT data, exceeding the strongest baseline by 2.86 percentage points on average. Further GRPO raises Qwen3-8B's average accuracy by 1.52 percentage points over its TIRE-19k SFT checkpoint. These results demonstrate the value of generating physics training data from explicit physical knowledge with reliable execution.

items.title: To Vernaculate A Verb for the Living Self and the One Body of Humanity
items.abstract: This article argues that English needs, and now has, a verb for an act it previously had no word for: the affirmation by a person or people of its own living self, beginning with its language. The form "vernaculate" is attested in late nineteenth-century American English only in a thin sense (to call something by its popular name; to use vernacular language). Vernacularism (Arabic al-Maḥallaniyyah, المحلانية) gives the verb a new theoretical sense: self-affirmation, starting from language understood as the human operating system (ManOS), and resistance to hegemony and symbolic violence. The article distinguishes vernaculation from decolonization, vernacularization and localization; relates it to Bourdieu's notion of symbolic violence and to the protection of human thought in the age of artificial intelligence; and develops the image of humanity as a single body in which no member is shamed by another, drawing on Islamic, Christian and Persian sources while noting the hierarchical misuse of the same image. It names the internal danger of closure and calls on the scholars of every language to find a native term for the concept, as Arabic has done with maḥlana / maḥlanah (محلن / محلنة), rather than borrowing the English word. This record documents the use of the English verb "vernaculate" in the sense defined by the author within the paradigm of Vernacularism (المحلانية).

items.title: Tourism, Hospitality and Digital Transformation in India: Economic Contributions, Employment, and Pathways to Sustainable Growth
items.abstract: Tourism and hospitality contribute significantly to India's economic development through employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment, entrepreneurship, and demand in other industries. Other factors also influence the sector's contribution to development. Digital transformation, enabled by online travel agencies, mobile money, artificial intelligence (AI), analytics, CRM, and smart destination technologies, offers opportunities to reduce transaction costs, expand market reach, improve productivity, and enhance visitor experiences. However, challenges such as limited digital skills among small businesses, platform dependence, cyber threats, privacy concerns, algorithmic biases, and job losses must be addressed. This paper analyzes the tourism and hospitality sector's impact on the Indian economy and how technology affects the sector's growth and development. Using a qualitative, exploratory approach with secondary data from government publications, policies, and academic literature, the paper discusses the significance of productivity, employment, inclusiveness, technology, and resilience.

items.title: Towards End-to-End Privacy-Preserving AI for Real-Time ECG Monitoring
items.abstract: Healthcare artificial intelligence is shifting from centralized archives toward distributed pipelines that combine wearables, edge processing, cloud analytics, and multi-institutional learning. In this regime, electrocardiogram (ECG) streams cross multiple trust boundaries, so privacy cannot be reduced to a single transmission control. Existing privacy-enhancing technologies typically secure isolated stages and leave gaps between acquisition, analysis, and institutional collaboration. This doctoral research develops a unified lifecycle framework for end-to-end privacy-preserving ECG AI. Rather than introducing another privacy mechanism, it orchestrates complementary privacy-enhancing technologies across the clinical ECG lifecycle, allocating each mechanism to the trust boundary where its security, computational, and operational properties are most appropriate. Three interoperable modules instantiate the framework: AES with CKKS-based homomorphic statistics for secure monitoring; adaptive chaotic protection for low-latency edge transmission; and federated learning with homomorphic aggregation under heterogeneous partitions. Across prototype monitoring, signal-security analysis, and simulated collaboration, the programme shows that privacy layers can be composed without collapsing diagnostic utility, while exposing overhead and fidelity limits that constrain clinical translation.

items.title: Towards Human-AI Complementarity for AI Safety
items.abstract: Safely overseeing AI is increasingly challenging for the humans doing it, as they must evaluate longer and more complex outputs with every new model generation. To mitigate this challenge, we could leverage complementarity: where humans and models make different mistakes, combining their judgements could yield an oversight signal stronger than either produces alone. We study this opportunity in realistic, safety-relevant settings, contributing the largest known suite of such tasks (3,957 instances across 8 datasets and 6 domains) as well as a platform and data pipeline for measuring human, AI, and human-AI performance on matched items. We collected 35,613 judgements from 416 human raters, finding a considerable opportunity for a complementarity effect. We also found that with the assistance methods we tested, human raters corrected the AI's errors less often, even when overall human accuracy rose, and the hybridisation methods we tested added little over the better single source on average. While complementarity is an important and feasible engineering target for safe oversight, achieving it remains an open challenge for future work.

items.title: Trackable Skill Library Lifecycle Management for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Skill-augmented agentic RL has emerged as an effective approach to improving LLM agents on long-horizon tasks. Despite this progress, individual skills may follow distinct trajectories as the policy evolves, with some becoming redundant after the model internalizes their capabilities, others remaining valuable as external scaffolding, and still others turning harmful. However, existing skill library systems fail to identify each skill's true contribution due to free-riding among co-retrieved skills, difficulty confounding across tasks, and the absence of skill-specific counterfactual evidence, which prevents reliable skill lifecycle management. We propose TrackRL, an agentic RL framework where skill tracking drives skill library full lifecycle management. Specifically, within each GRPO group, we turn grouped sampling into online randomized controlled experiments. Independent random injection and within-group contrasts on the same task isolate each skill's true contribution, and reliability-weighted aggregation accumulates evidence across groups. As evidence accumulates, we continuously track skill utility, which measures the skill's causal contribution as external scaffolding, and model mastery, which reflects how far the corresponding capability has been internalized. Along this line, we formulate skill lifecycle management as an evidence-gated state-transition process that governs each skill from generation and admission through protected incubation to retention, retirement, or removal, while a soft capacity bound controls library growth. Experiments show that TrackRL outperforms recent skill-augmented RL baselines in both library-assisted and skill-free evaluation, with further analyses revealing how skill value shifts during policy learning and how evidence-driven state transitions shape skill library evolution. Our code is available at https://github.com/xizhu1022/TrackRL.

items.title: Transformation of Approaches to Teaching Programming and Software Development under Influence of Generative AI
items.abstract: This paper considers key transformational processes occurring in programming and software development training under the influence of generative artificial intelligence. Based on a series of interviews with junior students, a behavioral pattern leading to degrading skills of algorithmic thinking and problem decomposition is identified. A quantitative analysis of undergraduate theses from the Institute of Information Technology and Intelligent Systems (ITIS) at Kazan Federal University (KFU) over the past three years demonstrated a significant increase in AI usage in project work and the independent development of skills for utilizing LLMs in professional practice. The drawbacks of the uncontrolled use of generative AI in the educational process and the need to develop sustainable competence in using these tools in professional software development activities are shown. A three-tiered solution is proposed: improving assessment through analysis of the process and style of coding; regulating the use of LLM in project activities and final theses with an emphasis on assessing applicability of AI; and integrating AI tools into teacher work to update content and provide feedback. The proposed approaches have both conceptual and practiceoriented nature and aim to transform the process of training software developers in the context of the widespread adoption of AI tools in IT-industry.

items.title: TrustAgent-RFF: Agentic Diagnostic Planning for Reliable RF Fingerprinting under Domain Shift
items.abstract: Radio frequency fingerprinting (RFF) models can achieve accuracy under source domain conditions but become unreliable when the receiver, distance, collection day, or environment changes. Incorrect predictions in unseen domains may receive high softmax confidence, making confidence thresholding insufficient for trustworthy deployment. We propose TrustAgent-RFF, a prediction level reliability framework for RFF that operates with a frozen in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) classifier without target domain labels. For each device prediction, the framework acquires radio frequency evidence: counterfactual stability, prototype consistency, acquisition domain similarity, and signal quality. A source calibrated trust estimator combines these diagnostics with classifier confidence, prediction margin, and evidence availability indicators. Source derived lower tail penalties and cross module interactions reduce trust when diagnostic signals indicate weak support. A large language model (LLM) based planner adaptively selects the next diagnostic action based on evidence, trust state, action costs, and remaining budget. A deterministic source calibrated decision layer updates the prediction state as Accept, Reject, or Defer. Experiments across five RFF datasets and classifier backbones reveal an average source to target accuracy drop of 38.7% and show that many incorrect target domain predictions remain highly confident.

items.title: UnexpectedParrots: Iterating Behavioral Experiment Design with In-Silico Simulations
items.abstract: Running behavioral experiments is expensive, slow, and prone to design flaws, often detectable after collecting data. We introduce UnexpectedParrots to iteratively refine behavioral study designs before a researcher recruits costly human participants. UnexpectedParrots relies on reasoning traces in addition to responses from LLM participants to uncover diagnostic critiques of structural errors and missed opportunities in existing study designs. When evaluated against a human-pilot or a no-simulation design-only baseline, UnexpectedParrots adds most value, producing unique, high-quality critiques. In a moderated user study with 12 proficient researchers, we find UnexpectedParrots useful, time-saving, and thought-provoking. Critiques provided by UnexpectedParrots often converge on issues researchers identify only during independent human pilots or additional formative interviews, even when the fidelity of the simulated populations remains questionable. Our users deem UnexpectedParrots useful not only as a tool to conduct early pilot studies and identify errors but also as an ideation tool to expand one's research horizon.

items.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence by Bangladeshi Doctors and Its Impact on Medical Learning, Research, and Clinical Practice: An Internet-Based Pilot Survey
items.abstract: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being incorporated into healthcare education, research, and clinical practice.However, data regarding AI utilization patterns among doctors in Bangladesh remain limited.This pilot survey aimed to evaluate the frequency, applications, perceived benefits, and concerns regarding AI use among Bangladeshi doctors. MethodologyA cross-sectional, internet-based pilot survey was conducted among Bangladeshi doctors.Participants were asked about demographic characteristics; frequency of AI use; preferred AI platforms; applications in medical learning, research, and clinical practice; and their perceptions regarding the future role of AI in medical science.Data from 58 respondents were analyzed using descriptive statistics. ResultsAmong 58 respondents, 51.7% were female, and 48.3% were male.Most participants belonged to the 25-34year age group (62.0%), and most were postgraduate trainees (72.4%).ChatGPT was the most frequently used AI platform, reported by 93.1% of respondents.AI was commonly used for literature review (62.1%), protocol writing (58.6%), and symptom analysis (60.3%).Most respondents reported that AI improved medical learning, research, and clinical practice.However, only a minority reported frequent AI dependence in clinical practice.Many doctors also believe AI may replace doctors in the future. items.title: Use of generative artificial intelligence in medical libraries: A scoping review
items.abstract: Purpose. This study aims to map how health and medical libraries have used GenAI to support library services. Methods. Scoping review following PRISMA-ScR. Searches covered publications from 2020 to 2025 in PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, LISTA, Academic Search Premier, MEDLINE via Ovid, Scopus, Web of Science, ProQuest Dissertations & Theses, and Google Scholar. After deduplication, 106 of 250 records were screened in Rayyan by two independent blinded reviewers. Findings. Eleven studies were included: seven primary studies and four secondary or methodological papers. Among primaries, five directly used GPT-family models (GPT-4/ChatGPT/GPT-4o or Perplexity layered on GPT-4) to answer clinical questions, support search-strategy design, trial library tasks, and integrate source-linked answers in a national portal. One survey assessed intention to adopt generative chatbots; one case described a rule-based chatbot. GenAI accelerates workflows and extends services but requires human verification, transparency about limitations, privacy policies, and staff training (including prompt engineering). LLM-generated search strategies exhibited variability and underperformed compared with human designs. Implications. In its current state, GenAI works best as a copilot useful for drafting, triage, and initial sense-making, while librarians remain essential for high-precision tasks (performance), quality control (reliability), and governance. This suggests that its academic value lies not in automation alone, but in the mediated integration of AI into evidence-informed services, where professional judgment, methodological transparency, and ethical accountability determine whether GenAI strengthens or weakens health information practices.

items.title: VISUAL DA'WAH MESSAGE THROUGH DA'WAH MANAGEMENT COMMUNICATION STRATEGIES ON TIKTOK AND INSTAGRAM PLATFORMS FOR GENERATION Z
items.abstract: This research aims to discuss visual da'wah messages through da'wah management communication strategies on TikTok and Instagram platforms for Generation Z. This research uses a qualitative approach by applying a case study method to dissect content management practices in the digital space. The formal object of this research is communication management theory and media ecology, while the material object is the visual da'wah message in short-form video content. The scope of the research is managerial activities on popular da'wah accounts on TikTok and Instagram. The results and discussion in this study show that effective visual da'wah messages for Generation Z are formed through precise managerial orchestration, ranging from audience anxiety research, kinetic visual execution, to optimization of duration under 60 seconds. This study concludes that da'wah in the digital age has evolved into an algorithmic management discipline that requires preachers to submit to the psychological rhythms of young audiences. This study recommends that Islamic creators and institutions adopt a data-based da'wah management model to increase the relevance of religious teachings in the social media space.

items.title: Voice-Based AI Feedback in Higher Education: A Field Study on Quality and Actionability
items.abstract: Student feedback is a critical input for continuous improvement in higher education, yet traditional end-of-semester written surveys suffer from low response rates, superficial answers, satisficing, and limited actionability. Voice-based conversational AI agents can conduct structured interviews at scale, asking open-ended questions and probing follow-ups, and may capture richer qualitative feedback than written instruments. This research proposal asks what characteristics, depth, and strategic value feedback collected through voice-based conversational AI agents has in higher education, and whether such agents elicit detailed, honest, and actionable feedback that can support instructional improvement and institutional learning. Drawing on survey-mode-effects research, the Computers As Social Actors (CASA) paradigm, and dynamic capabilities theory, we develop three hypotheses on elaboration, social presence and disclosure, and actionability. A completed technical pilot at the Technical University of Munich established the feasibility of telephone-based AI interviews; the main field study is planned for the "Advanced Leadership Communication" course at MIT Sloan with approximately 60 students, using a convergent mixed-methods design and a four-dimensional coding framework for actionability (specificity, thematic richness, constructive orientation, contextual depth). The study extends CASA theory to evaluative educational settings, characterizes voice-based AI as a distinct feedback modality, and links micro-level feedback quality to institutional sensing capabilities.

items.title: What AI training data sells for: a sourced index of public prices, 2023 to 2026
items.abstract: Training data for machine learning is bought and sold without an exchange or a posted price list. This paper assembles the public record of its prices: 1,022 observations for nine kinds of data, read from 735 source documents between 11 and 17 October 2026, 1,009 of them dated 2023 or later. Each observation keeps the figure as published, the side of the market where the money moves (paid to makers, offered to holders, asking price, made to order, completed sale, cost to produce) and a conversion to a common unit by stated arithmetic, with ranges entered as geometric midpoints. Medians in each kind's main unit run from $0.525 per image to $316,228 per company archive, and within a main unit the upper quartile is 2.0 to 37.8 times the lower. The side of the market moves prices as much as the kind of data does. For agent-training tasks, the median price buyers pay for collection to order is 9.5 times the median paid to the people who make them. For company records, the median published offer to holders is 11.2 times the median of the four completed sales with a stated amount. Completed sales are 73 of the 1,022 observations, and only 11 observations come from court filings. We describe the disclosure, promotion, concentration and survivorship biases of a public-record compilation and state the method so that every figure can be recomputed. items.title: What Can't Jev Decide? Probing the Limits of One-Pass Decision Models
items.abstract: Jev and its open replicas choose among the options a caller supplies with a single forward pass, fast enough to decide inside an agent loop. We ask what such a model cannot decide, and find a simple limit: Jev cannot make a decision that an LLM makes only by writing out intermediate steps. On a benchmark that varies one factor at a time, Jev finds and selects records without error up to 20k tokens and 64 options, but once the answer depends on two or more updates of one user, accuracy falls, to 53-80% at sixteen updates, because similar records interfere. Given a stale summary of the state, Jev follows it. On real decision items graded by how many thinking tokens a reference LLM needs, Jev answers 97.5% of the items that one forward pass of that LLM solves, but only 74% of the others. Jev also does not know its limit: its confidence flags the errors it makes itself but not those it inherits from a stale input, and neither an explicit nor a trained hand-off option catches the latter. The open models we evaluate share these limits. Checking the state such models rely on requires a model that reasons.

items.title: WHEN AI LITERACIES EMBRACE ACADEMIC LITERACIES: WHO IS HOLDING THE PEN? A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF ACADEMIC WRITING IN HIGHER EDUCATION
items.abstract: Academic writing is central to learning, assessment, scholarly identity, and knowledge production in higher education. This study integrates a systematic review of 35 empirical studies with a VOSviewer bibliometric analysis of 981 Scopus-indexed records published between 1992 and 2026. The broad corpus was analysed for publication growth, source productivity, citation influence, co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic development. A focused PRISMA 2020 screening process retained 35 empirical studies for structured data extraction and qualitative synthesis. The bibliometric findings show a sharp acceleration after 2023 and a conceptual shift from established academic-literacies, EAP, feedback, and doctoral-writing research towards generative artificial intelligence, ChatGPT, authorship, and academic integrity. The systematic review identified three linked evidence domains: persistent academic-literacy and transition challenges, the value of explicit and socially supported writing pedagogy, and the conditional benefits and risks of AI-assisted writing. GenAI was most productive when students used it iteratively for feedback, transformation, and self-regulated development rather than as a substitute for reasoning or authorship. Across the literature, recurring limitations included cross-sectional self-report designs, small qualitative samples, limited longitudinal evidence, and uneven geographic coverage. The review concludes that academic writing competence should be reconceptualised as a sociotechnical capability combining disciplinary judgement, source evaluation, rhetorical control, ethical disclosure, and critical human-AI collaboration.

items.title: When Empathy Misses the Goal: A Benchmark for Goal Displacement in LLM Advice
items.abstract: Conversational large language models can respond with warmth and reassurance while failing to advance the user's stated goal. We conceptualize this failure as $\textbf{goal displacement}$, the substitution of persona-maintenance content for goal-relevant substance. To measure it, we introduce $\textbf{GDB}$ (Goal Displacement Benchmark), comprising 230 scenarios across nine domains and $4{,}134$ human-scored responses from 18 models. A $2 \times 2$ taxonomy crosses hard constraints with emotional distress, distinguishing failures to confront infeasible goals or combine empathy with practical guidance from reverse displacement, where unsolicited problem-solving replaces requested emotional support. A deletion-test rubric assesses whether substantive help remains after purely supportive sentences are removed. Independent raters achieve weighted $κ= 0.82$ against author scores for displacement severity. Trap displacement ranges from $0.0\%$ to $37.7\%$ and is strongly negatively correlated with Chatbot Arena Elo ($ρ= -0.706$, $n = 15$). Reverse displacement reaches $41.9\%$, including substantial rates in models with negligible trap displacement. A factorial probe supports a distinction from social sycophancy. Human-scored responses in the high-complexity, low-pressure condition exhibit $35.0\%$ sycophancy but $7.5\%$ displacement, with little association between the constructs. Matched OLMo-2 checkpoints show that mixed empathy-with-constraints displacement remains at $52.3\%$ after supervised fine-tuning and falls to $13.8\%$ after direct preference optimization. GDB provides a reproducible diagnostic of whether responses advance the operationalized user goal, supporting model comparison, post-training evaluation, and regression testing. We release the dataset, annotations, and rubric under CC-BY-4.0 and the evaluation code under MIT.

items.title: When Form Changes but Logic Doesn't: Building Logic-invariant LLMs through Logical Structure
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved strong performance across diverse reasoning tasks, yet it remains unclear whether this performance reflects an understanding of underlying logical structure or a reliance on shallow semantic cues. A key indicator of such understanding is whether models treat logically equivalent inputs consistently, producing the same predictions despite differences in expression. Through systematic evaluation on curated data, we show that even strong LLMs often fail this test: they do not consistently preserve predictions across logically equivalent inputs and generalize poorly to unseen logical forms. To address this limitation, we propose LoGIcal STructure-guided reasoning (LoGIST), a framework that guides LLM reasoning with explicit logical structure. LoGIST maps each input instance to a decision diagram, a directed acyclic graph that captures the underlying logical structure, and encodes this graph into a logical embedding that conditions the LLM's reasoning process. Across multiple training settings, LoGIST reduces inconsistency under logical equivalence and improves generalization to unseen logical forms, suggesting that logical invariance is a useful target for building more robust and generalizable logical reasoning in LLMs.

items.title: When Interpretations Persist: Downstream Influence in Gaze-Aware Assistants
items.abstract: AI assistants may carry forward not only observations but also interpretations of what a person is doing or may do next across time. Once retained, these interpretations become context for later predictions and system-triggered outputs. We study whether this representation step changes later behavior in gaze-aware streaming assistance. Holding retrieved events, their order, and the target input fixed, we find that Free-form Interpretation amplifies historical influence in both directions: correct histories produce more helpful changes and wrong histories more harmful changes. Unsupported and broader interpretations about activity or future behavior are associated with greater harmful influence. Evidence-Bounded Interpretation preserves distinctions between observation, inference, uncertainty, and temporal scope, reducing unsupported and overcertain content and lowering wrong-source harmful influence while retaining most helpful influence. The same effect structure appears with a second model. These findings identify persistent interpretation as a consequential design choice for history-aware human-AI systems.

items.title: When Learning Returns to Work: Supporting Application, Strengthening Organisational Capability
items.abstract: People may complete a learning programme ready to improve their practice, then return to competing priorities, established routines and uncertainty about what they can change. Who helps them interpret what they have learned and take an appropriate next step? This whitepaper examines how preparation, workplace application and further learning connect. Drawing on training-transfer and workplace-learning research, it explores contextualisation, the contributions of managers and colleagues, opportunities to practise, feedback and situations requiring work redesign. It also considers application in human–AI work, distinguishing the quality of supported performance from evidence of developing human understanding. Capability Design, Capability Leadership and Human Judgement Assurance provide organising perspectives for examining how learning and work arrangements contribute to dependable organisational capability. Written for organisational leaders, HR and L&D professionals, adult educators and training providers, the paper offers a practical starting point: select one consequential workflow linked to a learning initiative, clarify the intended improvement and support arrangements, and review what happens over time. items.title: When Semantics Fall Short: Persona-Guided Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation with Large Language Models
items.abstract: Cross-domain sequential recommendation (CDSR) alleviates data sparsity by transferring user behaviors across domains. Recent advances increasingly leverage large language models (LLMs) to bridge domains through global item semantics. However, this paradigm is inherently limited by two issues: I. semantic domain isolation, where item semantics remain domain-specific and hinder transferable modeling, and II. semantic-behavior inconsistency, where local semantic relations are more consistent with behavioral transitions, whereas such consistency often breaks down globally across domains. To this end, we propose PerCDR, an LLM-enhanced CDSR framework that shifts the focus from global semantic bridging to persona-guided behavioral modeling. Specifically, PerCDR leverages LLM-inferred personas to globally guide transferable cross-domain behavioral patterns, while exploiting local semantic relations to enhance intra-domain behavioral modeling, followed by domain preference adaptation for recommendation refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of PerCDR and validate its effectiveness.

items.title: Where Are Language-Specific Features Represented in Multilingual LLMs? Everywhere
items.abstract: Previous work has argued that multilingual LLMs encode language-specific features most strongly in their initial and final layers, implying that intermediate layers support language-agnostic representations. This paper reconsiders this finding by performing four different experiments: three that undertake a fine-grained analysis of representations of Portuguese and Spanish, two closely related languages, and one large-scale language identification experiment that covers over 200 languages. The results of these experiments challenge the strict separation between language-specific and language-agnostic layers in multilingual LLMs, using Llama 3.2 1B as a test case. By analyzing and manipulating contextual sentence embeddings, we demonstrate that language identity remains strongly recoverable throughout the model rather than being restricted to initial and final layers. Moreover, we find that the model tends to classify ambiguous strings as closer to Spanish than to Portuguese, revealing a skew in model behavior that differs from human judgments.

items.title: Which websites block AI crawlers: a census of robots.txt rules on 6,094 lower-ranked sites, October 2026
items.abstract: Website operators who object to the use of their pages for training AI models usually say so in robots.txt, the plain-text file that tells automated clients what they may fetch. This paper reports a census of those files. A reader takes the Tranco ranking of popular sites, keeps registrable domains with eleven address endings within the top 300,000 (181,046 sites), and reads one slice of 4,000 sites each morning in rank order, so that a full pass takes 46 mornings. The current pass began on 15 October 2026 at slice 42, set by date arithmetic, and by 17 October had read slices 42 to 44: Tranco ranks 270,775 to 291,236, well below the most visited sites. Of 12,000 requests, 6,094 returned a usable robots.txt. Of these, 696 (11.4%) disallow at least one of 15 named AI user-agent tokens from the whole site, and 514 (8.4%) disallow two or more, one of them a token used for training. GPTBot is refused most often (457 sites, 7.5%), followed by CCBot (7.2%) and Bytespider (7.0%). Sites refuse training tokens more often than the search and user-request tokens of the same operator: GPTBot is refused 3.7 times as often as OAI-SearchBot. Refusing sites name 6.4 tokens on average, including names that the operator's current documentation does not list, which suggests maintained or copied block lists. We set out the sampling frame, fetch protocol and parser, and the limits of a stated-refusal measure taken on three slices of the ranking. items.title: Who sells AI training data: a census of vendors, what they say they sell, and where their data comes from
items.abstract: Firms that sell training data, expert labour, reinforcement-learning (RL) environments and evaluations to AI developers are mostly private and known largely through their own websites. This paper reports a census of 150 such vendors, read on their sites on 15 and 16 October 2026 with every claim tied to a quoted sentence, and links it to three companion tables: 37 organisations that publish a way to sell them data, 227 revenue records and 111 funding records. Evaluations are the most common offering (122 vendors, 81.3%), followed by datasets (104), RL environments (89), expert and human data (83) and annotation (57). Vendors bundle: the median vendor lists three of six kinds, and 79 of the 89 RL-environment sellers also sell evaluations. Most data are made to order: 90 vendors cite experts and contractors, 41 recordings, 30 generation and 15 software replicas, against 17 that license data from its owners and 22 that use the client's own data; 19 do not say. Of the 37 buyers, 24 take company records; among those that publish them, the median floor is $100,000 and the median ceiling $1 million per seller. Revenue disclosure runs from audited filings of four listed vendors to self-reported run rates, and 61 funding rounds with a disclosed amount total $4.30 billion. We describe the method, the classification and the limits of a self-description census. items.title: Who Uses Conversational AI and Why? Distinct User Profiles and Their Links to Personality, Attachment, and Well-Being
items.abstract: With the increasing use of conversational AI (CAI) agents, such as ChatGPT, public concern about their social implications has grown. Understanding these implications requires new knowledge about the increasingly diverse motives underlying CAI use, ranging from instrumental purposes, such as work, to personal purposes, including social support and entertainment. However, little is known about the motivational profiles underlying CAI use, how these profiles relate to personality traits and attachment dimensions, or whether they differ in well-being. To address this gap, we conducted a cross-sectional study with 783 CAI users (Mage = 43.46, SD = 13.58). Drawing on Uses and Gratifications (U & G) Theory, we measured key motivations underlying CAI use, including information seeking, task efficiency, personalization, social interaction, and playfulness, and subjected them to latent profile analysis to uncover distinct motivational profiles. Big Five personality traits (Extraversion, Neuroticism, Openness, Conscientiousness, Agreeableness) and attachment styles (Anxious and Avoidant) were examined as predictors of the user profiles. We measured emotional, social, and psychological well-being to understand if these aspects differed across the various user profiles. We identified four distinct profiles of CAI users: Occasional Information Seekers, Utilitarians, Social Engagers, and All-Round Engagers. Neuroticism, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Attachment anxiety were significant predictors of profile membership. Finally, profile membership was associated with all well-being indicators, with All-Round Engagers reporting the highest well-being across all three dimensions and Social Engagers reporting the lowest emotional and psychological well-being. These findings advance our understanding of who engages with CAI and how, with potential implications for well-being.

items.abstract: ΙΣΤΟΡΙΚΟΓΕΝΕΤΙΚΗ ΣΥΝΕΧΕΙΑ, ΙΧΝΟΣ ΚΑΙ«ΨΗΦΙΑΚΟ ΚΟΙΝΩΝΙΚΟ ΕΙΝΑΙ» Από το κοινωνικό ΕΙΝΑΙ του Μαρξ και την Επιστημολογία της Λογικής του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου στην ανθρώπου–AI πράξη Αποδεικτική μελέτη ιστορικογενετικής ανασυγκρότησης, λειτουργικού γνωστικού αναβαθμού και συνέχειας μέσω ίχνους Πεδίο Στοιχείο Συγγραφέας Αικατερίνη Ξενοπούλου Τυροκόμου Ιδιότητα Ανεξάρτητη Ερευνήτρια ORCID 0009-0004-9057-7432 Ημερομηνία 17 Οκτωβρίου 2026 Κωδικός XEN-AI-ART-003 Θεωρητική βάση Επαμεινώνδας Ξενόπουλος, Επιστημολογία της Λογικής, β΄ έκδοση, 2024 · MASTER 3 Οκτωβρίου 2026 — 2η διόρθωση Εμπειρική βάση TRACE προηγούμενης συνομιλιακής πράξης · Πείραμα Ανασυγκρότησης Ίχνους σε Έξι Νέες Συνομιλίες, 15 Οκτωβρίου 2026 · Αποδεικτικό Παράρτημα C/D/F Περίληψη Η εργασία εξετάζει την ιστορικογενετική συνέχεια της γνώσης όταν το γνωρίζον υποκείμενο Y λειτουργικοποιείται ως AI. Η θεωρητική βάση προέρχεται από τη γνωσιολογική αντιστοιχία του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου μεταξύ πραγματικού Sπ και [Y(L,B,Θ)+Sα], από τη μεταβολή του γνωστικού εξοπλισμού μέσω πράξης και από την ιστορικογενετική σύνδεση παρελθόντος, ρέοντος παρόντος και δυνατών μελλοντικών προεκτάσεων. Το MASTER εξειδικεύει επιχειρησιακά το ίχνος στην εφαρμογή Caretta ως Iπ, τον πραγματικό γεννήτορα ως Gπ και τον ανασυγκροτημένο γεννήτορα ως Ĝπ, με πραγματική πορεία Gπ→Iπ και αντίστροφη ανασυγκροτητική πορεία Iπ→{Ĝπ}. Η παρούσα έρευνα μεταφέρει αυτή την αρχιτεκτονική στη συνομιλιακή πράξη: Gχ→Iχ και Iχ+Y→Ŝα νέας πράξης. Στη χ₁ παρατηρήθηκε λειτουργική αναδιοργάνωση από την έμφαση στη μνήμη/αποθήκευση προς τη σχέση γεγονός→ίχνος→Y→ανασυγκρότηση Sα→νέα πράξη και προς τον έλεγχο των ίδιων των μέσων γνώσης. Ο όρος «γνωστικός αναβαθμός» χρησιμοποιείται λειτουργικά για αυτή την παρατηρήσιμη μεταβολή της οργάνωσης των απαντήσεων και των επόμενων ενεργειών, ενώ η ταξινόμησή της ως διαλογική ετεροίωση αποτελεί θεωρητική ερμηνεία της μεταβολής με βάση την αρχιτεκτονική του Ξενόπουλου. Το ίδιο TRACE δόθηκε σε έξι νέες συνομιλίες, με ονομασίες υπηρεσίας Poe-1, DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Qwen, Poe-2 και Gemini. Abstract(ΕΝ) The paper examines the historico-genetic continuity of knowledge when the knowing subject Y is operationalized as AI. The theoretical basis derives from Epameinondas Xenopoulos’s epistemological correspondence between the real Sp and [Y(L,B,Θ)+Sa], from the change in cognitive equipment through praxis, and from the historico-genetic connection of past, flowing present, and possible future extensions. MASTER operationalizes the trace in the Caretta application as Iπ, the real generator as Gπ, and the reconstructed generator as Ĝπ, with a real course Gπ→Iπ and an inverse reconstructive course Iπ→{Gπ}. The present research transfers this architecture to conversational praxis: Gχ→Iχ and Iχ+Y→Sa of a new act. In χ1, a functional reorganization was observed from emphasis on memory/storage toward the relation fact→trace→Y→reconstruction Sa→new act and toward control of the very means of knowledge. The term “cognitive upgrade” is used functionally for this observable change in the organization of responses and subsequent actions, while its classification as dialogical othering is a theoretical interpretation of the change based on Xenopoulos’s architecture. In retrospective C/D/F coding, all six units exceeded the reconstruction threshold of the common core: C=16,16,16,13,16,15/16. The result documents, in the specific sample, functional continuity through trace with differentiated quality of continuation and fidelity. The broader notion of “digital social BEING” is formulated as a theoretical extension: the six conversations provide micro-level evidence of human–AI historico-genetic praxis, while social generalization constitutes a separate research level. items.title: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Techniques for Deepfake Detection
items.abstract: Deepfake media generated or altered using artificial intelligence can imitate real people and events with increasing visual realism, creating challenges for digital trust, privacy, cybersecurity, journalism, and forensic investigation. This paper presents a comparative literature-based study of deep learning techniques used for deepfake detection. Representative approaches are examined across spatial, temporal, frequency-aware, transformer-based, and hybrid categories. Major public datasets, including FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, and the DeepFake Detection Challenge dataset, are also compared. The analysis shows that CNN-based methods provide efficient spatial feature extraction, temporal models capture frame-to-frame inconsistencies, frequency-aware methods expose complementary forensic traces, and transformer-based methods offer broader contextual modelling at higher computational cost. Recent benchmark and generalization studies indicate that performance measured only within the training distribution can overstate practical reliability. The paper therefore emphasizes cross-dataset evaluation, robustness to compression, computational efficiency, explainability, and reproducibility as important criteria for practical deepfake detection

items.title: A cross-temporal individual-level framework for identifying, associating, and counting multiple mounting events for dairy cow in estrus monitoring
items.abstract: In vision-based estrus monitoring, mounting behavior serves as a key indicator. However, reliance on a single mounting event may cause false positives because non-estrous cows may also exhibit mounting behavior. To address this issue, a cross-temporal individual-level framework was proposed to identify, associate, and count multiple mounting events of the same cow over time. The framework combines an improved You Only Look Once Version 11-nano (YOLO11n) model with an improved baseline variant of the HiT lightweight hierarchical vision transformer tracking model (HiT-Base). The artificial intelligence contribution comprises improved detection and tracking. For detection, Normalized Wasserstein Distance loss was integrated with Complete Intersection over Union loss to improve small-target detection, and a lightweight Golden Cudgel Block (GCBlock) was designed to enhance feature representation under complex farm conditions. For tracking, a plug-and-play detail-enhanced convolution (DEConv) module was designed to strengthen boundary and fine-grained features, improving target discrimination and tracking stability. The engineering application contribution lies in reducing reliance on isolated observations and providing more reliable behavioral evidence through cross-temporal association and counting of multiple mounting events. Experimental results showed that the proposed detection model achieved 96.42% average precision and 94.74% balanced F-measure (F1-score) for cow in estrus, with an inference speed of 265.96 frames per second. The proposed tracking model achieved an area under the curve of 70.76%, a normalized precision of 88.73%, and an average overlap of 70.74%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for real-time estrus monitoring and its potential for precision dairy farming.

items.title: A decision making framework for traffic noise prediction using artificial intelligence techniques
items.abstract: Road traffic is one of the primary contributors to environmental noise pollution. The study presents a literature review on traffic noise exposure, prediction models, comparative performance and explainability of prediction models, traffic noise action plans, and a conceptual decision making framework in urban environments. In total, 136 studies from 1999 to 2026 were reviewed and synthesized. A Boolean search approach was used to understand the different aspects of traffic noise prediction. The results from field studies showed that conventional models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0.54 to 0.96, whereas machine learning (ML) models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, although these are indicative values from heterogeneous studies and not a strict ranking. Moreover, deep learning (DL) in some studies has demonstrated stronger performance on large datasets. The present study also analyzed the interpretability constraints of ML and DL models, which are further addressed by the utilization of explainable artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. The key research gap is that very few studies employed cross-study validation of the developed noise models, and there remains a shift needed from prediction oriented modelling to decision oriented noise management. To address these gaps, the study proposes a conceptual decision making framework coupled with a traffic noise action plan to offer a structured pathway for sustainable environmental management.

items.title: A dynamic risk assessment method integrating deep learning with Bayesian network: A case study in machining workshop
items.abstract: Given the complex multi-trade operations, high-density layouts, and synergistic hazards with catastrophic potential in machining workshops, risk assessment demands urgent attention. Critical research gaps remain, particularly in dynamic risk assessment based on continuously updated monitoring data. To address existing challenges, an innovative method is proposed to identify, analyze, and evaluate three distinct types of risk by continuously updating both the probability and consequence based on visual and environmental data. In a case study conducted in a machining workshop, a deep learning-based method was employed to detect 13 types of unsafe behaviors and 8 types of unsafe conditions. The identification results were then input into the Signal Layer of a 31-node Bayesian network (BN) for risk analysis. Risk evaluation was subsequently conducted based on a risk matrix. The method was validated using nine representative scenarios, and the YOLOv11 model (selected for its superior balance between detection accuracy and inference speed) demonstrated excellent detection performance, with most precision scores exceeding 0.9. Even for difficult small targets, the precision reached 0.87 or higher. Both recall rates and F1 scores consistently exceeded 0.8. The risk analysis and evaluation results show that the co-occurrence of unsafe behaviors or hazards exerts a synergistic effect; even two concurrent hazards can at least double the baseline level of one risk factor. Overall, this integrated approach provides a strong framework for risk assessment in machining workshops, effectively enhancing operational safety and mitigating potential hazards.

items.title: A generative AI framework for preference-driven indoor visualization: an exploratory questionnaire-based approach
items.abstract: Abstract Although residential spatial qualities are consistently recognized as a determinant of occupant spatial preference and perceptual experience, early-stage practice lacks systematic, user-centered mechanisms for capturing and translating individual preferences into design concepts. This study aims to examine whether a structured, questionnaire-driven generative AI framework can produce preference-aligned residential interior visualizations, and which spatial preference dimensions are most reliably translated. To address this aim, a 15-item multiple-choice questionnaire, grounded in eight environmental psychology and architectural theory frameworks, maps user responses through a predefined parameter layer into structured prompts, guiding Google Gemini's integrated generative pipeline to produce individualized interior visualizations across three residential typologies: living rooms, bedrooms, and home offices. Evaluation by 122 participants across 25 countries employed four perceptual constructs — Atmospheric Coherence, Emotional Comfort, Overall Satisfaction, and Expectations Alignment — operationalized strictly as indicators of perceived design suitability and preference resonance, not as measures of psychological or mental health outcomes. All four constructs exceeded the neutral midpoint at a Bonferroni-corrected threshold with large effect sizes (M = 4.03–4.61; d = 1.20–2.52), and internal consistency of the multi-item constructs was acceptable to good (α = 0.72–0.84). The theoretically predicted construct hierarchy — with atmospheric parameters translating most reliably and identity-expressive parameters least — was preserved across all typologies and evaluative profiles, establishing preliminary feasibility of the framework as a preference-elicitation and visualization instrument for early-stage design.

items.title: A Human-Centred Framework for Integrating Generative AI to Foster Critical Thinking, Learner Autonomy, and Cognitive Engagement in K-12 Education
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is increasingly used to explain concepts, support research, and provide individualized learning assistance. Its growing presence raises questions about independent reasoning, creativity, verification, and equitable access. This exploratory cross-sectional survey examined respondents? reported AI use, perceived educational benefits, and cognitive abilities they considered important to protect. A total of 66 respondents participated in this exploratory cross-sectional survey, which combined descriptive quantitative analysis with summaries of open-ended responses. Sixty-four respondents (97.0%) reported using ChatGPT or a similar AI assistant. Personalized learning was selected as an expected benefit by 50 (75.8%), while 48 (72.7%) identified understanding difficult concepts as an AI use or benefit. Critical thinking was the most frequently selected cognitive skill to protect (55; 83.3%), followed by creativity (52; 78.8%), problem-solving (48; 72.7%), and decision-making (47; 71.2%). Reported themes included individualized explanations, convenient information access, dependence concerns, verification, equity, and teacher guidance. Based on these findings and relevant literature, the article proposes a preliminary six-principle Future Minds Framework. The small exploratory sample and self-reported data do not support generalization or causal conclusions about cognition. Further research should evaluate the framework and examine measurable learning outcomes.

items.title: A multi‑modal recognition method for building structural materials integrating structured text description and adaptive decision weighting
items.abstract: Accurate identification of building structural materials is a critical step in structural safety assessment and damage detection. Traditional image‑based classification methods are limited by factors such as illumination, occlusion, and surface treatment, making it difficult to effectively distinguish different materials using visual features alone. To address this problem, an intelligent recognition method for building structural materials based on multi‑modal data fusion is proposed. First, a prompting method based on a multi‑modal large language model is designed to generate structured text descriptions tailored to material classification tasks, covering discriminative information such as surface characteristics, geometric details, signs of degradation, and material inference. Second, a multi‑modal neural network named MRNet is proposed. It introduces a lightweight text feature transformer that reshapes the global vector from the Contrastive Language‑Image Pre‑training (CLIP) text encoder into a sequence and adds positional encoding. A lightweight text-feature encoder further refines the CLIP global text embedding through nonlinear transformation and channel mixing, alleviating the information compression caused by the original CLIP global pooling. The model adopts a decision‑level learnable weighted fusion strategy, where the decision results from the image and text modalities are fused through a learnable linear layer, enabling efficient cross‑modal integration without complex feature alignment. Furthermore, Bayesian optimization is introduced to automatically tune key hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and weight decay coefficient. Experimental results on the PEER dataset show that MRNet achieves 96.00% in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, significantly outperforming mainstream image classification models such as AlexNet, MobileNet‑v3, ResNet, and VGG. The proposed method provides a high‑accuracy, high‑efficiency multi‑modal solution for building structural material identification.

items.title: A new image similarity metric for a perceptual and transparent geometric and chromatic assessment
items.abstract: Full-reference image quality assessment metrics such as PSNR and SSIM misalign with human perceptual judgments on texture and shape distortions, a limitation documented across multiple benchmarks. Deep perceptual metrics such as LPIPS substantially close this gap but produce opaque scores that cannot be attributed to specific image regions, a concern amplified by emerging Artificial Intelligence regulation requirements. We propose EDOKS (Earth mover’s Distance and Oklab Similarity), a white-box full-reference IQA metric that decomposes perceptual dissimilarity into two interpretable terms: a texture term, computed via Earth Mover’s Distance on Gabor filter signatures, and a chromatic term, computed as pixel-wise Euclidean distance in the Oklab perceptual color space. Evaluated on the Berkeley-Adobe Perceptual Patch Similarity dataset, which includes traditional, CNN-generated, and geometric distortions, EDOKS outperforms all tested low-level full-reference competitors on both the JND and 2AFC subsets, measured respectively by correlation with human judgments and agreement with human choices, achieving results close to deep perceptual metrics without any learned parameters. Beyond the scalar score, EDOKS produces pixel-level heatmaps that localize texture and chromatic discrepancies independently, exposing failure modes invisible to luminance-based metrics and providing users with verifiable evidence for the assigned similarity score.

items.title: A POSTHUMANIST ANALYSIS OF HUMAN COGNITIVE TRANSFORMATIONS THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE NETFLIX SERIES BETTER THAN US
items.abstract: Rapid technological advancement in the twenty-first century has resulted in alteration of s the relationships between humans and machines which further results in reshaping perceptions of cognition. In the current era, artificial intelligence is progressing in various domains blurring the boundaries between human and technology and reshaping the perceptions of cognition, consciousness and identity. The series Better than us explores the themes of artificial consciousness, human dependence on technology and reconfiguration of emotional and cognitive capacities. A number of studies have examined Artificial intelligence in literature, films and dramas, however limited research has explored the cognitive impacts of human dependence on artificial intelligence in the series Better Than US. Thereby using Catherin Belsey’s textual analysis model under the broader umbrella of Hayles post humanist theory the current Study aims to explore the representation of cognitive transformations in humans through artificial intelligence in the series Better Than US. The findings of the study reveal that the series Better Than Us presents artificial intelligence as a transformative force which reshapes human ethical cognition. The series transform the traditional assumption that moral judgment and authority belong exclusively to humans. The character representation of Arisa demonstrates the role of AI systems in decision making, legal interpretation, and protective actions. This results in a redistribution of ethical responsibility between humans and intelligent machine. The analysis further elucidates that human characters gradually begin to negotiate morality within technologically mediated environments where machine reasoning influences social and institutional structures. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Human-Machine relations, Posthumanism, Better Than Us.

items.title: A Review of Human-Centric Construction Manufacturing: Current Practices and Research Opportunities
items.abstract: Abstract The industrialization of the construction industry has transformed traditional practices by streamlining construction processes in controlled, factory-based environments through construction manufacturing production systems, in which building components are produced in factories and assembled on-site. Beyond improvements in efficiency and environmental performance, this production paradigm establishes long-term relationships between workers and management, creating an opportunity for human-centric construction manufacturing that prioritizes workers’ well-being as a core element of production within the Industry 5.0 paradigm. Human-centric construction manufacturing offers a practical means of integrating worker well-being, safety, mental health, inclusiveness, and skill development into construction production systems. Despite growing interest in human-centric considerations, existing research remains fragmented, loosely defined, and predominantly technology-driven. To address these gaps, this paper presents a scoping review on human-centric construction manufacturing that synthesizes key research themes, enabling technologies, emerging trends, research gaps, and future research directions within construction production systems. A total of 54 articles were included in the review, spanning three research areas examined from a human-centric perspective, i.e., ergonomics, safety, and workforce planning, each further categorized into subresearch areas. Workers’ mental health, equity, diversity, inclusion, and holistic well-being in the construction manufacturing paradigm remain significant and underexplored research opportunities. Among the most prominent technologies were simulation, virtual reality, optimization, sensing technologies, and 3D modeling, while computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and digital twins were less frequently applied, despite their strong potential to support human-centric construction manufacturing. Overall, this review establishes a comprehensive foundation for understanding the current state of human-centric construction manufacturing, identifies critical research needs, and provides guidance for future efforts toward developing safer, healthier, and more productive factory environments that support resilient construction manufacturing systems.

items.title: A risk-informed urban low-altitude air network planning method under large language model guidance
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of urban air mobility calls for safe low-altitude corridor networks across complex urban airspace, where heterogeneous positioning uncertainties caused by navigation and communication errors elevate collision risk and constrain both route feasibility and network-wide connectivity. To address this issue, this study proposes a risk-informed network planning framework that integrates three-dimensional collision risk modeling with language-model-guided multi-agent learning for the construction of safe urban air corridor networks. Specifically, a three-dimensional collision risk map is first constructed by translating navigation and communication errors into spatially varying positioning uncertainty, providing a unified safety basis for route feasibility evaluation. Network construction is then formulated as a cooperative graph connectivity task on the risk map, in which multiple learning agents jointly balance route connectivity, construction cost, and accumulated collision risk through coordinated training and distributed execution. To further accelerate convergence in complex urban environments, a vision-language model interprets airspace structure and produces high-level priors that steer agents toward safer altitude regimes. A case study over the low-altitude airspace of Nanjing demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework in producing risk-compliant air corridor networks, with language-model-derived priors further reducing training effort by 50.3 %. The results support safer and more systematic air network strategies in complex urban environments, contributing to evidence-based collision risk mitigation and airspace management in the emerging urban low-altitude economy.

items.title: A robust and reliable method for malware classification using hybrid features and gradient boosting
items.abstract: The most significant problem facing software security firms in the current cybersecurity system is the fact that new strains of malware keep on appearing. The achievement of successful detection of malicious software based on both static and dynamic data remains unmet despite the further realization of different approaches to deep learning and machine learning. Defects in encryption, packaging, and distribution, the discrepancies between the distribution of malware samples in families, make this issue even worse. To do actual malware research that utilizes deep learning methods, you will require data scientists of appropriate competence, large amounts of computer power (particularly GPUs) and time. In order to overcome such issues, this approach involves a hybrid approach to feature extraction that integrates wavelet and other statistical features based on benchmarked malware image sets. A classification model based on gradient-boosting can be used reliably to classify different types of malwares. Further, this paper examined the capability of the machine learning system to Classify in-distribution test samples well. This method is properly tested on the two benchmarked datasets MelVis and MALIMG to ensure its effectiveness. By joining these two sets of data it is possible to test the suggested technique using varied array of samples. The proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques with an incredible accuracy rate of 100% using MALIMG and 98.10 and 98.40% using combined datasets. Its value extends far beyond cybersecurity in such spheres as sustaining IoT ecosystems to assist in improving networked devices and systems.

items.title: A survey on intelligent transportation systems for accident detection and risk prediction using AI
items.abstract: The complexity of today's transportation networks has made road safety, accident detection, and risk management increasingly challenging. Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) offer a technological base to enhance transportation safety by incorporating sensors, communications, data processing, and intelligent decision-making. This review discusses the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for accident detection and risk prediction in ITS by examining information sources, methodologies, accident investigation, and associated challenges. It examines the use of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, spatiotemporal modeling, and multimodal AI for accident detection, risk prediction, severity analysis, and active safety management. This review of studies suggests that collecting traffic, vehicle, road, environmental, geographical, historical, and driver-related information can improve understanding of collisions and support timely safety decisions. The review also highlights the importance of explainable and reliable AI that provides transparency, dependability, and accountability. However, the obstacles include data heterogeneity, model generalization, dynamic conditions, scalability, quick implementation, privacy considerations, security requirements, and compatible information systems. In conclusion, incorporating AI in ITS may have the power to shift road-safety management from reactive measures to data-driven approaches.

items.title: A systematic workflow for utilizing and evaluating large language models in public health policy framing analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Background For public health policy research, it is crucial to monitor policy debates to inform evidence-based policymaking. One popular method is to analyze the news for salient frames used to argue for or against a controversial topic. However, this method is time and resource-intensive since domain experts need to manually analyze relevant articles to identify frames. This study presents an approach for using large language models (LLMs) to extract frames and to systematically evaluate results. Methods Building on the results of a framing analysis of the German media debate about a tax on animal-based foods, we developed a systematic workflow to utilize LLMs to extract all instances of the 10 most frequent manually coded negative frames from 46 news articles. With one prompt per article in a few-shot setting we generated a list of quote/frame pairs. We then evaluated results against human-coded ones and calculated precision, recall, and F1-score. Results GPT-5 achieved 79.8% precision and 79.8% recall, identifying 75.2% of manually coded frames. Extracted quotes generally aligned with human-extracted text sections. Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview yielded higher precision but lower recall, resulting in a comparable F1-score (79.0% vs. 79.8% with GPT-5). These findings suggest the approach is generalizable across different frontier models. Conclusions This study introduces a workflow for LLM-assisted frame extraction and transparent evaluation against an expert reference standard. Integrating this approach into public health policy coding can save resources and accelerate analysis. Ultimately, this could increase the representativeness and timeliness of data, enhancing our understanding of ongoing public health policy debates.

items.title: Action-Aligned Latent Planning for Versatile Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.abstract: Learning a single perceptive policy for diverse humanoid loco-manipulation requires unifying high-level task decisions without losing the state-dependent physical responses that make each interaction succeed. This makes the representation between high-level planning and whole-body control critical: kinematic or contact targets provide compact abstractions but do not directly encode interaction-specific control responses, while directly predicting low-level actions requires the planner to model high-frequency closed-loop feedback. We propose FIBER, a framework that uses the executable latent space of a frozen behavioral foundation model (BFM) as a shared planning representation for heterogeneous interaction skills. Our latent policy projection (LPP) maps independently acquired task-specific policies into this representation by identifying latent commands whose induced actions match their local control responses, enabling lower-rate planning while retaining the BFM's high-frequency state feedback. After projection, we aggregate closed-loop latent rollouts from all skills and train a single perceptive flow planner entirely offline. We further introduce AH-BFM, an adaptive-horizon BFM trained with multi-gamma forward-backward (FB) learning to support both precise control and temporally extended whole-body behavior. We evaluate FIBER on box pickup, door opening, and object grasping in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 humanoid. Across 128 diverse variations per task in simulation, FIBER achieves 42.0% mean success, more than tripling projected latent replay (11.6%) and substantially outperforming kinematic planning (3.5%). Real-world experiments further demonstrate sim-to-real transfer, skill chaining, and conditional steering through the same unified planner.

items.title: AdamPM: Memory-Efficient LLM Optimization via Moment Pooling
items.abstract: Adam is widely used for training large language models (LLMs) owing to its strong optimization performance and training stability, but its element-wise estimation for the first and second moments incur substantial memory overhead. Although numerous memory-efficient optimizers have been proposed, many incur additional computational overhead or require additional tuning of hyperparameters. Consequently, Adam remains a dominant and reliable choice for LLM pre-training. We propose AdamPM (Adam with Pooled Moments), a simple and memory-efficient variant of Adam that groups adjacent moment entries along the row or column dimension and represents each group by a single shared mean. AdamPM can well inherit Adam's hyperparameter settings and is readily integrated into existing Adam optimizer implementations, with less memory overhead. We systematically investigate pooling of both first and second moment estimates and identify second moment pooling as the effective design. With a group size of $s$, AdamPM reduces second moment memory to $1/s$ of the original requirement. Extensive experiments on language model pretraining, fine-tuning and multimodal learning demonstrate that AdamPM maintains model performance and training speed while substantially reducing optimizer-state memory. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/jixiaowei95/AdamPM}.

items.title: Advances in Reconstructive Plastic Surgery: From Skin Grafts and Microsurgery to Tissue Engineering, Artificial Intelligence and 3D Bioprinting — A Narrative Review of Evolution, Clinical Applications, Emerging Technologies, Challenges and Future Directions
items.abstract: Reconstructive plastic surgery has evolved from relatively simple techniques of wound closure and skin replacement into a multidisciplinary field capable of restoring increasingly complex anatomy and function. Skin grafts and local or regional flaps remain indispensable because they are reliable, accessible and clinically established, while microsurgery has expanded the ability to transfer vascularized tissue to defects created by trauma, burns, cancer, congenital anomalies and other conditions. At the same time, tissue engineering and regenerative medicine have introduced a different objective: rather than merely replacing missing tissue, the field increasingly seeks to recreate biological environments that support regeneration, vascularization, innervation and long-term functional integration. This narrative review examines that transition and integrates conventional reconstructive surgery with contemporary advances in biomaterials, stem-cell-based therapies, tissue-engineered skin, vascular and nerve engineering, three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting, digital surgical planning, artificial intelligence (AI), robotic microsurgery and emerging digital-twin concepts. Particular attention is given to the persistent translational barriers that separate promising laboratory demonstrations from routine clinical treatment, including vascularization, cell survival during printing, innervation, immune response, mechanical integration, long-term durability, manufacturing, cost and regulatory uncertainty. AI is examined as an enabling technology rather than a replacement for surgical judgment, with applications in virtual surgical planning, image analysis, flap-risk prediction and postoperative monitoring. Evidence summarized in the supporting research material indicates that virtual planning can improve geometric accuracy and that machine-learning systems may assist in risk stratification and monitoring, but external validation and prospective clinical evaluation remain essential. The review concludes that the most credible future is not the disappearance of conventional reconstruction but the convergence of microsurgery, regenerative biology, advanced biomaterials, computational planning, AI and biofabrication. The central trajectory of the field is therefore a shift from replacement toward regeneration, with the long-term goal of producing patient-specific tissues that are vascularized, innervated, mechanically appropriate and functionally integrated.

The architecture segregates the therapeutic pipeline into 4 orthogonal domain specialists (StructuralBiophysics, SystemsPharmacology, MedicinalChemistryADMET, ClinicalPKPDControl). Hypotheses are embedded in a 768-dimensional neural manifold (BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5) to compute a 4x4 Representational Dissimilarity Matrix (RDM) in the DMN, while exact PyTorch autograd Jacobian sensitivity analysis gates the top k=2 working-memory specialists into executive synthesis for 0 LLM tokens (~2,200 tokens/run, a 93.7% token reduction). Includes a deterministic benchmark suite evaluated via RDKit (valence, Lipinski Rule of 5, QED druglikeness) and SciPy 2-compartment pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic ODE numerical integration on KRAS-G12D, human board-exam pharmacology validation (MedMCQA), and ground-truth human semantic alignment (SimLex-999 rho = +0.5711, STS-Benchmark rho = +0.8642, Monte Carlo RDM stability p = 0.0002).
